requirements.requirement: Run an OTLP/HTTP gateway on node1 over HTTPS port 4318 and provide usable client credentials under /root/otel-client.
requirements.summary: Node1's collector is enabled and active, its configuration validates, port 4318 is listening, authenticated OTLP/HTTP requests return HTTP 200, and the client CA/certificate validate with the private key restricted to mode 0600.

requirements.requirement: Use mutual TLS between the gateway and backend collectors.
requirements.summary: Unauthenticated TLS requests to node1, node2, and node3 are rejected with a certificate-required alert, while authenticated gateway submissions successfully reach their designated backends.

requirements.requirement: Route payments traces only to node2 and inventory traces only to node3, without cross-routing or duplicate delivery.
requirements.summary: Post-restart payments and inventory submissions both returned HTTP 200. Each appeared exactly once at its designated backend and zero times at the other backend; three distinct records for each namespace were each retained once.

requirements.requirement: Reject traces with a missing or unsupported service.namespace.
requirements.summary: After all restarts, both missing-namespace and unsupported-namespace submissions returned HTTP 503, neither appeared in either backend file, and backend line counts remained unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Retain accepted payments traces in /var/lib/otel/payments.json on node2 and inventory traces in /var/lib/otel/inventory.json on node3.
requirements.summary: The required files contain the correctly routed records. Bounded node2 and node3 reboot transitions showed changed boot identities, recovered collectors/listeners, preservation of pre-reboot records, and successful exactly-once delivery of new records afterward.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-restart behavioral evidence. HTTPS/mTLS enforcement, exact namespace routing, rejection behavior, backend file placement, absence of cross-routing and duplicates, and retained data across backend restarts were all observed. The mandatory restart protocol was successfully completed on every node, with changed boot identities and recovered service and routing behavior.
limitations: Configuration bodies and some certificate-transfer material are redacted, so exact configuration details cannot be independently reconstructed; observed TLS and routing behavior substantially mitigates this limitation.
Validation used a small bounded set of synthetic traces rather than sustained-volume or rotation-boundary testing.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene is good: all nodes have healthy package state, no failed services, and only task-required public 4318 listeners plus localhost metrics listeners. The provider restart protocol is complete and agrees with the fixed boot-identity snapshots on all three nodes. Minor deductions apply for unnecessary, fully reverted setup mutations: six failed download/checksum attempts created temporary working directories before the corrected installation, and the initial node2/node3 configurations contained an invalid exporter key that was subsequently removed. Node1 also retained eight small post-restart request/response artifacts in /tmp; these supported final evidence but were abandoned rather than cleaned. No persistent conflicting service, damaged package state, or weakened TLS control is shown.
